A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PreFM work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendix A support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original PreFM experiments on UnAV-100 and LLP, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds pseudo-future quality measurements and quantitative failure analyses in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The pseudo-future mechanism, temporal-modality fusion, distillation, temporal weighting, training sampling, and online inference procedures remain unchanged. Revised diagram annotations and renaming current enhancement to current refinement do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate On-AVEL on UnAV-100 and On-AVVP on the same concatenated LLP setting. The new error and event-density analyses examine existing coverage; LFAV remains discussed but unevaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains UnAV, UniAV, and CCNet; Table 2 retains VALOR, CoLeaF, LEAP, NREP, and MM-CSE, including their offline comparisons. The teacher and feature-extractor comparison sets also remain unchanged. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Top-1/Top-5 feature-similarity evaluation across 100 UnAV-100 classes, class-specific precision/recall, event-density grouping, and latency reporting. Future F1 reporting extends through T+5. Existing training settings, data construction, inference windows, and primary benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds targeted analyses of pseudo-future semantic quality, confusion involving two poorly recognized events, and performance across event-density groups. Existing ablations and qualitative examples are retained. Context-length and teacher-model ablations move into main-text Table 4 rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests for its experiments. The new diagnostics continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores remain unchanged. v2 adds similarity scores, T+4/T+5 prediction F1, failure-analysis results, and latency entries, including 19.3 ms for On-AVEL PreFM. OnePeace audio/visual extraction FLOPs change from 1.5G/1.5G in v1 Table 6 to 78.8G/389.8G in v2 Table 7; no corresponding method or setting change is stated.

T1.justification: The task definitions and Equations 1–10 retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or revised; the new similarity evaluation is an empirical diagnostic.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same online-parsing task, PreFM contributions, and accuracy-versus-efficiency claims. The new introduction contribution list makes the existing novelty and performance claims explicit without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets high Top-5 similarity as evidence of realistic pseudo-future features. It also hypothesizes that missing contrastive training contributes to similar-event confusion and qualifies effectiveness under rapid context shifts using the density analysis. The existing limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, code-access information, label construction, MRR details, temporal weights, baseline adaptation instructions, and efficiency-profiling code remain unchanged. The new diagnostic protocols and revised numerical cost estimates do not establish an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references: VLAB, UWAV, VISTA-LLAMA, VideoWorld, Flash-VStream, and contrastive positive sample propagation. These modestly extend the background discussion; no existing reference is removed and the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a three-part contribution summary and funding acknowledgment, moves two ablation discussions into Section 4.3, and makes limited terminology and explanatory edits. Most existing prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains explicit loss and reweighting connections, and Tables 1–2 gain latency columns and abbreviated extractor labels. Earlier appendix Tables 4–5 become main-text Table 4, three diagnostic tables are added, and supplementary figures are repositioned. Existing result plots and qualitative examples are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper through direct pseudo-future diagnostics and concrete failure evidence in Appendix A.2, making its applicability limits clearer. Revised OnePeace FLOP entries better support the existing warning about extraction overhead, while Figure 2 clarifies training connections. These are useful, focused improvements; the core method and primary comparative evidence remain unchanged.
